# Best Espresso Machines

> Independent, research-based comparisons of home espresso machines for US kitchens. We compare published specifications, what ships in the box, machine class, footprint and live pricing across 32 machines. We do not physically test products, and we publish no star ratings because Amazon's product API returns no verifiable rating data for this category — we would rather show nothing than invent a number.

## Top picks (2026)

- **Best overall — Breville BES870XL Barista Express (~$685):** built-in conical burr grinder with dose control, 54 mm portafilter, 67 oz tank, 1,600 W, low-pressure pre-infusion. Grinder included, so it usually costs less than a comparable machine plus a separate grinder.
- **Best for milk drinks — Breville Bambino BES450BSS (~$300):** automatic microfoam steam wand with adjustable milk temperature and texture, compact footprint. No grinder, so budget for one separately.
- **Best value bean-to-cup — AMZCHEF Espresso Machine with Grinder (~$200):** built-in burr grinder with 44 settings, brew-temperature control 190–201 °F, 60 oz tank, cold-brew mode, descaling function. Newer brand, so long-term reliability is unproven.
- **Best one-touch — De'Longhi Magnifica Start (~$650):** super-automatic; grinds, doses and brews behind one button, 13 grind settings, 3 one-touch recipes. Lower ceiling than a semi-automatic, manual milk frother.
- **Best all-rounder — Ninja Luxe Café Premier 3-in-1 (~$599):** espresso plus 3 drip styles and 2 cold-brew styles, built-in burr grinder, dual automatic froth system including cold foam. Breadth over espresso depth.
- **Best capsule + coffee — Ninja CFN601 (~$280):** Nespresso original-capsule compatible espresso side (espresso, lungo, over ice) plus a 12-cup drip side. Cheap to buy, permanent per-cup capsule cost.
- **Best under $100 — CASABREWS 3700 Essential (~$100):** 1,350 W boiler, manual steam wand, stainless, only 5.7 inches wide. No grinder, small boiler.
- **Cheapest worth buying — Chefman CraftBrew (~$80):** 15-bar pump, 1.5 L removable reservoir, programmable shot volume, two baskets. Below this price you reach steam-driven machines that brew well under espresso pressure.

## How to choose

- **The grinder decides more than the machine.** You need a burr grinder — built into the machine or standing beside it. Blade grinders cannot produce an even espresso grind.
- **Bar ratings are marketing.** Espresso brews at roughly 9 bar at the puck; "15 bar" or "20 bar" is the pump's maximum rating and tells you nothing about the cup.
- **Milk is a real decision axis.** A manual steam wand gives control and latte art with a learning curve; an automatic frother gives a walk-away routine with less control.
- **Machine classes:** steam-driven (cheapest, well below espresso pressure), pump semi-automatic (you grind, dose, tamp), super-automatic (one button does everything), capsule (no control, ongoing cost).
- **Measure the counter** with the lid open and the tank removable, and check tank size if more than one person drinks coffee.

## Method

We start from every espresso machine we can source through Amazon's official product API (32 machines for this category), sort them by machine class rather than marketing copy, compare the specifications that change the cup — grinder, boiler wattage, brew-temperature control, steam wand, footprint, tank — and pick one winner per buying situation. We read manufacturer pressure claims sceptically. We do not run a testing lab, and we publish no ratings we cannot verify.
